title: After Tuesday's close: chips stepped back, health care stepped up
text: Monday's giant rally faded for chip stocks. NVIDIA fell 5.9% to $155.38 after its 31% jump, and AMD fell 8.9%. SPY slipped 0.5% and QQQ fell 2.0%, because QQQ holds more tech companies. At the same time, health care stocks rose: Eli Lilly gained 3.3% and Intuitive Surgical 4.4%. So the market did not fall apart. Money moved from one group of stocks to another. The market is closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, so there are only two short trading days left this week.

title: NVIDIA's risk score moved into High
text: NVIDIA closed at $155.38. That is about 36% below its high of the past year ($243.37). Its risk score went from 6.4 to 6.5 out of 10, which is just over the line into High. Huge moves in both directions, like +31% then -6%, are what a high score warns about. Jensen Huang is scheduled to answer questions from three House committees on December 1, which could bring new headlines.

title: Chip makers fell more than the big AI users
text: The companies that build parts for AI dropped the most today. AMD fell 8.9%, Vertiv 6.7%, Broadcom 4.0% and TSMC 3.8%. The big companies that use AI moved much less: Alphabet fell 1.1%, Amazon 1.2%, and Microsoft actually rose 0.7%. Broadcom is now only about 4% above its lowest price of the past year ($289.77).

title: Health care had its best day in a while
text: Health care stocks on the Nasdaq rose about 4.1% on average, the best sector today. Sanofi, a big French drug company, agreed to buy Insmed for $175 per share in cash, about $41 billion. Eli Lilly closed at $1,410.12, only about 4% below its high of the past year. Lilly's risk score is 3.2, which is Low.

title: Lesson 65: What is sector rotation?
text: A sector is a group of companies that do similar work, like chips or health care. Sector rotation is when investors sell one group and buy another. Today is a good example: chip stocks fell while health care stocks rose. The total market only dipped a little, because the money did not leave, it moved. This is one reason to own different kinds of companies. When one group has a bad day, another group may have a good one, and that smooths out the ride.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices, 52 week ranges, beta and company size come from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) after Tuesday's close. Analyst price targets and company ratios come from FMP for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE Aerospace; the free plan does not include them for Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly or Intuitive Surgical. The 10 year Treasury yield comes from Alpha Vantage. News comes from the Associated Press, SEC filings and the NYSE. Risk scores and scenarios are simple math, not predictions. Nothing here is advice to buy or sell.
